text: Fill in the missing terms about regulation of gene expression.
questions: In the lac operon, *allolactose* acts as the inducer that binds the repressor and releases it from the operator.
Strong lac operon transcription also requires the cAMP–CAP complex, which binds the promoter only when *glucose* levels are low.
In eukaryotes, histone *acetylation* loosens chromatin and activates transcription, while deacetylation silences genes.
Methylation of cytosine in promoter *CpG* islands is an epigenetic mark that silences gene expression.
Steroid receptors bind hormone response *elements/Elements* to regulate transcription of their target genes.

overallFeedback.feedback: The lac operon illustrates two-level control: negative (repressor released by the inducer allolactose) and positive (cAMP–CAP binds only when glucose is low). Eukaryotic regulation adds epigenetic layers — histone acetylation opens chromatin, CpG methylation closes it — and transcription factors, including steroid receptors binding hormone response elements, that explain how the same genome produces different cell types.
